To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electric field distribution in the brain during TTFields treatment depends on the tumor dielectric characteristics, the presence of a necrotics core in the tumor, the tumor geometry, the position of TTFields transducers, and the thickness of the cerebellum and the cerebrospinals fluid on the convexities of the brain.

the electric field parameters EA, E50% and VE150%, as well as SAR parameters SARA, SAR50% and SAR20% facilitate the comparison between the models derived from various anatomical and electrical conditions.
the dielectric properties and geometry of adjacent tissues and GTV, as well as the position of the electrodes, affect the electric field and energy deposition in the tumor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical parameters that can be used to optimize TTFields therapy for glioblastoma.
the physical characteristics of TTFields for human gliobastoma.
the development and implementation of a personalized approach for the delivery of TTFields to the brain, and our work may be used to guide TTFields treatment planning in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TTFields treatment is an effective therapy against glioblastoma, but that the efficacy of the therapy may be influenced by the physical characteristics of the brain and tumor, as well as the position of the TTFields array.
the distribution of TTFields in the GTV is affected by multiple factors and that a personalized approach to TTFields planning is necessary.
the distribution of TTFields in the brain and the corresponding rate of energy deposition can be influenced by various patient‐related factors and the geometry of a glioblastoma tumor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the physical characteristics of the electric field and the rate of energy deposition are influenced by the dielectrics of adjacent tissues, the geometry of the brain and tumor, and the position of the transducer arrays.

the electric field parameters EAuc and VE150, as well as the rate of energy deposition parameters SARAUC and VSAR7.25, can be used to evaluate the distribution of the TTFields in the GTV and surrounding tissues.
the physical characteristics of TTFields for human gliobastoma is dependent on the dielectric properties of the adjacent tissues, tumor geometry, and the position of the TTFields arrays.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electric field parameters EAuc, VE150, and VE95% are most sensitive to the geometry of the brain, the presence or absence and size of the necrotic core, and the position of the TTFields electrodes.

the distribution of TTFields and energy deposition in the tumor and surrounding tissues are dependent on a number of physical parameters, which can be used to develop a personalized approach for treatment.
the distribution of TTFields in the brain is highly variable and depends on a number of factors, which can be used in future studies for the optimization of treatment planning.
